document: ET-8b gen0 + G3 — the HELD-OUT result, and the contaminated one it replaces

G3_STATE_DEPENDENCE.gate: fraction of episodes whose decision-2 state differs between arms >= 0.30
G3_STATE_DEPENDENCE.why_it_matters: 8a §9 could not test accumulation because generation 1's training states were BYTE-IDENTICAL to generation 0's — a single fixed decision meant the prior never changed what it later saw. 0.879 is the measurement that the loop fixed that. There IS something to accumulate on.

⚠️_THE_NUMBER_THE_CHAIN_PRINTED_WAS_CONT.why_wrong: the gen0 head was fitted on tasks < 226 and the loop ran ALL 300, so 225 of the 300 evaluation tasks were in the head's own training set.
⚠️_THE_NUMBER_THE_CHAIN_PRINTED_WAS_CONT.reading: the all-300 figure is dominated by memorisation — the head is 24 points better on tasks it was fitted on than on tasks it was not. +17.3 is the result; +35.0 is an artifact of my own run design.
⚠️_THE_NUMBER_THE_CHAIN_PRINTED_WAS_CONT.how_it_was_caught: +35 was far larger than 8a's +13 on the same environment. A result that beats its own predecessor by 3x is a reason to check the split, not to report it. I had avoided exactly this in 8a by evaluating on slice 4 only, and then did not carry the rule into the loop chain.

next: gen1 — a head fitted on the states gen0 PRODUCED, which now exist and differ from the base's on 87.9% of held-out decision-2 states. And the gen1 run must evaluate HELD OUT.
